title: Boundedness of a continuous logarithm near a nonzero limit
statement: Let E,L : ℝ → ℂ. Assume E is continuous on (1,2), L is continuous at 1 within [1,∞), L(1) ≠ 0, and exp(E(s)) = L(s) for every 1 < s < 2. Then there exist 0 < ε ≤ 1 and C ≥ 0 such that ‖E(s)‖ ≤ C whenever 1 < s < 1+ε.
lean_statement: ∀ (E L : ℝ → ℂ), ContinuousOn E (Set.Ioo 1 2) → ContinuousWithinAt L (Set.Ici 1) 1 → L 1 ≠ 0 → (∀ s : ℝ, s ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 → Complex.exp (E s) = L s) → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ε ≤ 1 ∧ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ s : ℝ, 1 < s → s < 1 + ε → ‖E s‖ ≤ C
